➡️ **Referral for pelvic floor physical therapy evaluation and management.**

This 32-year-old woman presents with primary infertility of 15 months’ duration, but no clear organic cause has been identified. All evaluated hormonal parameters (FSH, LH, estradiol, testosterone, mid-luteal progesterone, TSH) are normal — ruling out overt hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis dysfunction, anovulation, thyroid disease, or hyperandrogenism. Thus, the dominant, actionable diagnosis is not a hormonal or anatomical disorder, but a neuromuscular–behavioral condition impairing vaginal penetration — i.e., vaginismus, best conceptualized as a subtype of genito-pelvic pain/penetration disorder (GPPPD), with pelvic floor hypertonicity as its physiological substrate.

- Involuntary pelvic floor muscle tension causing speculum examination to be aborted.  
- Coital discomfort reported.  
- Inability to tolerate vaginal instrumentation.  
- Normal hormonal profile (FSH, LH, estradiol, testosterone, mid-luteal progesterone, TSH) rules out endocrine causes of anovulation or hypoestrogenism that might secondarily cause vaginal atrophy or spasm.  
- Normal pelvic ultrasound excludes structural pelvic pathology that could provoke reflexive guarding.  
- Absence of galactorrhea or abnormal bleeding makes hyperprolactinemia an unlikely primary driver of the penetration failure.  

[GAPS]  
- Male partner’s semen analysis result is pending — critical to rule out male factor infertility.  
- HSG result is pending — needed to confirm tubal patency.  
- Serum prolactin level remains unmeasured — though clinical features argue against it, formal exclusion requires measurement.  
- Menstrual history (cycle regularity, duration, flow) is unavailable — limits full assessment of ovulatory function despite normal mid-luteal progesterone.  

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Vaginismus (Genito-Pelvic Pain/Penetration Disorder with pelvic floor hypertonicity)
